request.spec:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rate calendar is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests. To get there I also had to change how crews behave when their lead leaves the sheet, which the request didn't mention — details below.

**Rate calendar** (`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/rates.ts`)
- There's a new table in the Rates section with one row per grade and one column per month of the sheet's today's calendar year. Each cell (`rate-month-<grade>-<YYYY-MM>`) shows the rate in force on the 1st of that month, or `n/a` when there is none.
- It uses the existing `rateOn` lookup, the same one behind the current-rate column, so to-dates and parent-sheet rates are handled the same way. It changes when the sheet's today moves into a new year.
- This part needed no server or database changes.

**Change to crews**
Scenario 3 transfers Cam, crew C1's lead, to another sheet. It then expects C1 to still exist with an empty lead and Ada holding 100.00 in C1's pool. Before, the app deleted any crew whose lead left. I changed that, because the test requires it:
- **Database:** a new migration, `V93__crew_lead_leaves.sql`, lets a crew's lead be empty.
- **Server:** when a lead leaves the sheet, their crews are kept with no lead (`CrewService.personLeaving`). Crew lists, merging and sheet cloning now cope with a crew that has no lead. In `PoolService`, a crew with no lead is still listed as a pool, shared among its remaining members (any rounding remainder goes to the first member). A crew is left out of the pools only when none of its people are left.
- **Front end:** a crew with no lead shows an empty lead, and its due-total is just its members' totals.
- I updated the comments that described the old behaviour.

You may want to review this, since it changes what happens to a crew when its lead leaves.
